name: maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition

Nothing here builds a view/projection matrix, so the previous 'Gfx_ComputeViewTransform' label was wrong; the routine is the camera follow/offset step of the camera module (called from the same sites as Camera_SetupFromRecord).

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList
signature: u32 maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList(CameraWork* cam, int targetId, CameraTargetRecord* rec)
summary: Resolves a camera target record. When rec->f_58 == 0xC it walks the up-to-0x20 visible target slots of the current screen block (0x2AF*4 stride, 0x1C-byte records) and, for each candidate, calls Camera_IsCandidateVisible + maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkEntry, committing the first match with Camera_SetupFromRecord. Otherwise it walks the scene-node list, picks the node whose action record at +0x54 matches targetId and applies Field_ApplyNpcActionState to it.
evidence: Named callees Camera_IsCandidateVisible, maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkEntry, Camera_SetupFromRecord, Field_SceneNode_GetPosition and Field_ApplyNpcActionState now fix both branches, but the function does two unrelated things (camera slot commit and NPC action apply), so 'UpdateTargetList' is only half right - kept as maybe_ with a corrected summary rather than promoted.

name: Camera_UpdateWorkList
summary: Drains the deferred camera work-request list at +0x163C: for every queued request it re-resolves the referenced camera target slot (0x1C stride, 0x20 slots) or path entry (0x10 stride, 0x10 entries) of the current screen block and commits it with Camera_SetupFromRecord; then it unlinks and frees the request nodes, leaving the list empty.
evidence: Only caller is the now-named Gfx_InitScreenViews, and the per-request commit call is the named Camera_SetupFromRecord. The previous summary ('advances each work entry and rebuilds the list') was wrong: the loop only validates the referenced entry and frees the request node, it never advances an entry. The name is vague but supported.

name: maybe_Ui_DragScroll_Update
summary: Three-state touch-drag/scroll handler for a list window. State 1 resolves the scene object under the touch point, detaches the widget (Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy), plays the drag animation on it and hides the shared overlay element; state 2 accumulates the pointer delta into the window's +0xC4/+0xC8 offsets and, when the pointer is back on its origin, calls the window's vtable+0x54(4) and stops the drag (Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState); any other state does nothing.
evidence: Named callees now pin the mechanics (Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy, Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState, maybe_Overlay_HideElementClass) and the offsets written are the same +0xC4/+0xC8 delta pair used by the field actors. Whether the accumulated value scrolls the list or drags an icon cannot be decided from the code, so kept as maybe_.

summary: While the actor is not busy (f_1C5 clear) this reads the player's movement vector through the named Input_ReadDigitalMoveVector and, in game modes 1-4, snaps it to the dominant axis and doubles the step; the resulting X/Y step is added to the actor's movement delta at +0xC4/+0xC8. With a zero vector it just plays the idle animation.
evidence: The stick reader is now the named Input_ReadDigitalMoveVector and the animation stop is the named Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState; the same +0xC4/+0xC8 delta is written by the named ActorAction_UpdateMove (0x3ADFAC), which confirms this is the input half of the movement pipeline. The 'stick' wording is slightly loose (the helper is the digital move vector) but the behaviour is right.

summary: Moves the player actor across a map-cell boundary: bails out while the two game-work mode bytes at +0x44/+0x45 or the UI transition state are busy, converts the actor grid position (+0x78/+0x7C) to a cell coordinate through func_00643CE4 and compares it with the cached cell, then either performs the cell switch (release trail, redraw, idle animation) or nudges the actor's +0xC4/+0xC8 position by the cell delta.

Named callees in both branches (maybe_Field_Actor_ComputeCellTransitionOffset, maybe_Gfx_Trail_Smooth, Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState, maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateScaleB, Ui_ObjectList_Begin/End) support the 'cell switch' reading, but the two mode bytes and the 0x643CE4 converter are still unnamed, so it stays maybe_.

name: Ui_TextLayer_SetColorByRatio
signature: void Ui_TextLayer_SetColorByRatio(UiTextLayer* self, void* text, u32 id)
summary: Picks a colour from the value/max ratio of a gauge cell and applies it to the text layer: computes (virtual +0x90)/(virtual +0x94)*100, compares it against the four thresholds in the constant block and writes one of the four colour words into the layer.
evidence: The four threshold constants (0x41C80000 = 25.0, etc.) and the four colour words are explicit and the setter is the named Ui_TextLayer_SetText; the 0..100 scale and the four-band selection are exactly what the code computes.

name: Ui_SlotGrid_SetIconIds
signature: void Ui_SlotGrid_SetIconIds(UiSlotGrid* self, u32 mask, u32* values)
summary: Writes the four slot icon ids, where bit 0..3 of mask selects for each slot whether the primary (values[0]) or the secondary (values[2]) value is used, then pushes all four to their text layers.
evidence: The bit-to-slot mapping and the 4 x Ui_TextLayer_SetText push are explicit, and the same f_30C..f_318 icon array is read by the sibling Ui_SlotGrid_ToggleSlotIcon, so the array's role is fixed.

name: Ui_SlotGrid_ToggleSlotIcon
signature: void Ui_SlotGrid_ToggleSlotIcon(UiSlotGrid* self, int slot, u32* value)
summary: Toggles the 'special' state of one slot: flips its flag at entry+0x1E4, updates the two linked panes' highlight bit 0, stores the new icon id into the slot's f_30C array entry and refreshes all four text layers.
evidence: Same icon array and text-layer push as Ui_SlotGrid_SetIconIds, plus the explicit flag flip and the two pane highlight writes; the concrete meaning of the flag is still unknown but 'toggle slot icon state' is what the body does.

name: Ui_Window_SetTabIcons
summary: Switches the four tab icons of a window between their normal and selected sprite: stores mode in f_50, picks the corresponding value from the global tab-icon block and pushes it to every tab whose type byte (+0x51+i) is 2 or 3.
evidence: The mode store, the four-iteration loop and the tab-type test are explicit, and the resulting value is pushed through the named Ui_TextLayer_SetText; 'icon' is an interpretation of the two-word value but consistent with the sprite/frame use in this UI module.
